raw:
Here are 10 hypotheses. They are based on standard MLP optimization behaviour and on the 100 single-seed probes.

1. **Raising alpha when alpha is already high (0.0167–1) helps less.** Over-regularization is what drives the losses. In probe #3, going from 0.129 to 1 cost 6–11 pp on all three datasets.
2. **Lowering alpha when alpha is high helps more.** This is the same over-regularization effect, approached from the other side.
3. **Adding depth when the learning rate is high (0.0774–1) helps less.** Deeper nets diverge at high learning rates. Probe #97 lost 51–68 pp on segment and vehicle, and probe #52 lost 14 pp on segment.
4. **Adding depth when depth is 1 helps more.** In the probes, going from 1 to 2 layers gave large phoneme gains (+2 to +5 pp), while going from 2 to 3 gave little.
5. **Raising the learning rate when it is low (1e-05 to 0.000129) helps more.** These models are undertrained within 243 epochs. Probe #30 gained on two datasets.
6. **Raising the learning rate when it is high helps less.** The model is pushed into instability.
7. **Lowering the learning rate when it is high helps more.** Stability recovers.
8. **Raising batch size when the learning rate is high helps more.** Larger batches reduce gradient noise and stabilize steps. Probe #70 gained up to +5 pp.
9. **Raising batch size when the learning rate is low helps less.** Fewer updates make undertraining worse. Probe #69 lost 1–9 pp.
10. **Raising width when width is low (16–40) helps more.** Width has diminishing returns, so capacity matters most when the network is narrow.
